answer:
The longest bridge in the world, by length of a single continuous span over water, is the **Lake Pontchartrain Causeway** in Louisiana, United States. The original section of this causeway opened on **August 30, 1956**.

A second, parallel stretch was added later and opened on **May 10, 1969**, but both together form the continuous structure that holds the record for the longest bridge/causeway over water (approximately 23.8 miles or 38.4 km long).

Overview Vocabulary
On August 30, 1956, the Lake Pontchartrain Causeway opened across Lake Pontchartrain, Louisiana. The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway is the longest continuous bridge over water in the world. The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway links the urban area of New Orleans, Louisiana, with the smaller communities on the north shore of Lake Pontchartrain. The roadway is 38 kilometers (24 miles) long, and supported by 9,500 concrete pilings. The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway benefitted residents on both sides of the bridge. People who worked in the city had their commute time reduced drastically. The bridge also increases business for retail stores and restaurants in towns on the north shore by allowing New Orleanians and tourists greater access.

Title: How long is the Lake Pontchartrain Causeway. It's the longest in the world
Chunks: 0,1,2,3
The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway in South Louisiana is the longest bridge in the U.S. and is the longest continuous bridge over water in the world.
The causeway consists of two parallel bridges spanning nearly 24 miles, measuring 126,122 feet.
Roughly 40,000 vehicles traverse acrossLake Pontchartrain Causeway daily and it takes 20 to 30 minutes to cross.

## Lake Pontchartrain Causeway holds Guinness World Record for longest bridge over water in the world
The first stretch of Lake Pontchartrain Causeway was opened in 1956 and the second was opened in 1969. The parallel bridges are supported by over 9,500 concrete pilings.
The bridge was designed with the purpose to connect the urban area of New Orleans with communities on the other side of Lake Pontchartrain like Metairie and Mandeville.
The causeway currently holds the Guinness World Record for the longest continuous span of bridge over water in the world, says IFLScience.

## Do people hallucinate while driving over Lake Pontchartrain?
When driving along Lake Pontchartrain Causeway, there reaches a point where there's no land in sight, only water and the stretch of concrete vehicles drive upon, for about eight miles.
While drivers may not 'hallucinate' in the literal sense, driving along the causeway can induce psychological stress, vertigo and spatial disorientation.
The monotonous scenery, view of expansive water and potentially high-risk fog has made some drivers report losing their sense of time, zoning out or even seeing things that aren't there, says MotorBiscuit.

## Louisiana is home to 5 of the 10 longest bridges in the U.S.
The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway is closed and waiting on an inspection to reopen in Metairie, La., on Monday morning August 30, 2021, after Hurricane Ida came ashore in Louisiana on Sunday August 29, 2021. Kenner07
Five of the 10 longest bridges in the U.S. are found in Louisiana. Here are the top 10 longest bridges:
1.   Lake Pontchartrain Causeway (Louisiana): 23.8 miles

2.   Manchac Swamp Bridge (Louisiana): 22.8 miles

3.   Atchafalaya Basin Bridge (Louisiana): 18.2 miles

4.   Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel (Virginia): 17.6 miles

5.   Mobile Bay Bridge (Alabama): 12.87 miles

6.   San Mateo-Hayward Bridge (California): 11.27 miles

7.   Bonnet Carré Spillway Bridge (Louisiana): 11 miles

8.   General W.K. Wilson Jr. Bridge (Alabama): 9.78 miles

9.   Louisiana Highway 1 Bridge (Louisiana): 8.26 miles

10.   Seven Mile Bridge (Florida): 6.79 miles
_Presley Bo Tyler is a reporter for the Louisiana Deep South Connect Team for USA Today. Find her on X @PresleyTyler02 and email at PTyler@Gannett.com_
_This article originally appeared on Shreveport Times:__Is Lake Pontchartrain Causeway a Guinness World Record for longest?_

The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway in South Louisiana is the longest bridge in the U.S. and is the longest continuous bridge over water in the world.
The causeway consists of two parallel bridges spanning nearly 24 miles, measuring 126,122 feet.
Roughly 40,000 vehicles traverse acrossLake Pontchartrain Causeway daily and it takes 20 to 30 minutes to cross.
texts.1:
## Lake Pontchartrain Causeway holds Guinness World Record for longest bridge over water in the world
The first stretch of Lake Pontchartrain Causeway was opened in 1956 and the second was opened in 1969. The parallel bridges are supported by over 9,500 concrete pilings.
The bridge was designed with the purpose to connect the urban area of New Orleans with communities on the other side of Lake Pontchartrain like Metairie and Mandeville.
The causeway currently holds the Guinness World Record for the longest continuous span of bridge over water in the world, says IFLScience.
texts.2:
## Do people hallucinate while driving over Lake Pontchartrain?
When driving along Lake Pontchartrain Causeway, there reaches a point where there's no land in sight, only water and the stretch of concrete vehicles drive upon, for about eight miles.
While drivers may not 'hallucinate' in the literal sense, driving along the causeway can induce psychological stress, vertigo and spatial disorientation.
The monotonous scenery, view of expansive water and potentially high-risk fog has made some drivers report losing their sense of time, zoning out or even seeing things that aren't there, says MotorBiscuit.
texts.3:
## Louisiana is home to 5 of the 10 longest bridges in the U.S.
The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway is closed and waiting on an inspection to reopen in Metairie, La., on Monday morning August 30, 2021, after Hurricane Ida came ashore in Louisiana on Sunday August 29, 2021. Kenner07

Overview Vocabulary
On August 30, 1956, the Lake Pontchartrain Causeway opened across Lake Pontchartrain, Louisiana. The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway is the longest continuous bridge over water in the world. The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway links the urban area of New Orleans, Louisiana, with the smaller communities on the north shore of Lake Pontchartrain. The roadway is 38 kilometers (24 miles) long, and supported by 9,500 concrete pilings. The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway benefitted residents on both sides of the bridge. People who worked in the city had their commute time reduced drastically. The bridge also increases business for retail stores and restaurants in towns on the north shore by allowing New Orleanians and tourists greater access.

The longest bridge in the world, by length of a single continuous span over water, is the **Lake Pontchartrain Causeway** in Louisiana, United States. The original section of this causeway opened on **August 30, 1956**.

A second, parallel stretch was added later and opened on **May 10, 1969**, but both together form the continuous structure that holds the record for the longest bridge/causeway over water (approximately 23.8 miles or 38.4 km long).
